ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-021", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: checkout-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 07:42 UTC)
Alerting service: checkout
Alert time: 2026-04-07T07:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-04-07T06:00:00Z to 2026-04-07T09:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-04-07T09:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-04-07T06:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate metric for checkout service to confirm anomaly.)
  Result: M-014: Change detected at 2026-04-07T06:15:00Z: mean 0.52 before, 14.6 after (373.6 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-014] checkout.error_rate_pct from 2026-04-07T06:00:00Z to 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.18 max=29.99 mean=13.43 last=29.66; mean=13.43. Change detected at 2026-04-07T06:15:00Z: mean 0.52 before, 14.6 after (373.6 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-04-07T06:15:00Z = 0.18 (first point after the change); 2026-04-07T06:15:00Z = 0.18 (lowest); 2026-04-07T08:00:00Z = 29.99 (peak); 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z = 29.66 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-04-07T09:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-04-07T06:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if the database connection pool is exhausted for checkout.)
  Result: M-012: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-012] checkout.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-04-07T06:00:00Z to 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=24.49 max=36.53 mean=29.46 last=26.21; mean=29.46. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-04-07T08:00:00Z = 24.49 (lowest); 2026-04-07T08:40:00Z = 36.53 (peak); 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z = 26.21 (last).
Step 3: metrics_query {"end": "2026-04-07T09:00:00Z", "metric": "restarts", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-04-07T06:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if checkout service has been restarting or crashing (could indicate OOM).)
  Result: M-018: Change detected at 2026-04-07T07:40:00Z: mean 0 before, 0.5 after (500000.0 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-018] checkout.restarts from 2026-04-07T06:00:00Z to 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0 max=3 mean=0.22 last=0; mean=0.22. Change detected at 2026-04-07T07:40:00Z: mean 0 before, 0.5 after (500000.0 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-04-07T06:00:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-04-07T07:40:00Z = 3 (first point after the change); 2026-04-07T07:40:00Z = 3 (peak); 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z = 0 (last).
Step 4: log_search {"end": "2026-04-07T06:30:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "deploy version start", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-04-07T06:00:00Z"} (asked because: Search for deployment or startup logs around 06:15 UTC when the error rate jumped.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 5: metrics_query {"end": "2026-04-07T09:00:00Z", "metric": "memory_pct", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-04-07T06:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check memory usage for checkout service to see if an OOM/memory leak is happening.)
  Result: M-016: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-016] checkout.memory_pct from 2026-04-07T06:00:00Z to 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=51.84 max=59.01 mean=56.12 last=54.49; mean=56.12. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-04-07T07:20:00Z = 51.84 (lowest); 2026-04-07T08:30:00Z = 59.01 (peak); 2026-04-07T08:55:00Z = 54.49 (last).
Step 6: log_search {"end": "2026-04-07T06:20:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "version deploy error started", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-04-07T06:10:00Z"} (asked because: Search checkout logs around the 06:15 UTC error rate jump for deployment or error details.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 7: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "memory leak out of memory OOM restarts mitigation mitigation steps"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for memory leak OOM issues.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-05-3 (similarity 0.85).
  [R-05-3] Memory leak and OOM kills - How to confirm (similarity 0.85): Look at how memory use moves between restarts. If it climbs steadily after every start and the platform reports that it ended the process for using too much, a leak is the likely cause. Compare against restarts with a different explanation, such as a rollout.
  [R-05-2] Memory leak and OOM kills - Symptoms (similarity 0.81): The service keeps being restarted by the platform, and it behaves worse each time it comes up before it dies again. Failures arrive in bursts around the restarts and then ease off briefly while the fresh instance is healthy.
  [R-05-5] Memory leak and OOM kills - Mitigation (similarity 0.80): Restart cycling hides the problem for a while, so scale out so each instance carries less load, and raise the memory limit as a stopgap. Capture a memory dump from an instance close to its limit before it is killed. Roll back if a release introduced the leak.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- downstream_timeout: Error rates jumped significantly starting at 06:15 UTC while database connection pools and memory usage remained stable, suggesting external dependency issues. (evidence: M-014, M-012, M-016)
- bad_deployment: An abrupt jump in error rate occurred without correlation to resource exhaustion, pointing towards a possible bad deployment or configuration issue. (evidence: M-014)
- memory_leak_oom: Service restarts were detected at 07:40 UTC, although memory percentage metrics remain steady. (evidence: M-018, M-016)
